body:
Forgive the naive question, as I don't understand snapshot and delta construction as well as I'd like. During snapshot construction, couldn't it choose to include the `NotCovered` cert in the club card anyway? Sure, no clients would know to look for it there, because they don't know that it was definitely visible yet. But once the next delta ships, and the clients believe that CRLite now _does_ cover the cert's SCT timestamp, they'd transparently start finding it already revoked in the existing snapshot clubcard.

Alternatively, could the construction system save the `NotCovered` cert in a small database, and include all such certs in the next delta update? (Actually now that I've written this down, I think it's equivalent to your first option, so feel free to ignore this paragraph.)

Great questions, let me explain the constructions in a bit more detail.

A clubcard encodes a subset R of a set U. Suppose we have a sequence of subsets `R_i ⊆ U_i`. Let `S_i = R_i \ R_{i-1}` (i.e. `S_i` is the elements of `R_i` that are not in `R_{i-1}`). In the snapshot and delta construction, the snapshot is a clubcard `C_0` that encodes `R_0 ⊆ U_0` and the deltas are clubcards `C_i` that encode `S_i ⊆ U_i` for `i > 0`. Given a snapshot and a sequence of deltas, you can evaluate `x ∈ R_i` by querying each of `C_0`, `C_1`, ..., `C_i` for `x`. Some of these queries may give a "NotCovered" result, indicating that `x` is not in `U_i`.

A clubcard for `R ⊆ U` includes a description of the set `U`. In CRLite that description is a list of tuples `(log_j, t_j)` where `log_j` is a CT log identifier and `t_j` is a timestamp cutoff. A certificate `x` is in `U` if and only if there is a `j` for which `x` has an SCT from `log_j` with a timestamp `t < t_j`.

The value `t_j` is one MMD less than the maximum timestamp that the CRLite aggregator saw in `log_j`. Because of the MMD offsets, the set of certificates `U'` seen by the aggregator is slightly larger than the set of certificates `U` described by the coverage metadata. Likewise, the set of observed revoked certificates `R'` is slightly larger than `R`.

The bug here is that we compute the difference sets `S_i` as `R'_i \ R'_{i-1}` rather than `R_i \ R_{i-1}`. In particular, the set `R'_{i-1}` includes some elements that are not in `R_{i-1}` and these are wrongly excluded from `S_i`.

We also use `R'_0` instead of `R_0` for the snapshot.

> During snapshot construction, couldn't it choose to include the NotCovered cert in the club card anyway? Sure, no clients would know to look for it there, because they don't know that it was definitely visible yet. But once the next delta ships, and the clients believe that CRLite now does cover the cert's SCT timestamp, they'd transparently start finding it already revoked in the existing snapshot clubcard.

So we do include the NotCovered certs in the snapshot. The problem with your suggestion is that SCT timestamps within one MMD period of one another are not strictly ordered. So suppose we have two clubcards, `C_0` and `C_1`, and suppose that `x` is not in `U_0` but it is in `U_1`. There are two possibilities
* `x` is in `U'_0` => if we were to bypass the coverage check then `C_0` would correctly report membership of `x` in `R'_0`,
* `x` is not in `U'_0` => `C_0` has no information about the membership of `x` in `R'_0` and would give a "random" result if we asked.

We cannot distinguish these cases because timestamps are not strictly ordered. If they were, then we could infer which of these two cases applied based on how the coverage metadata changed between `C_0` and `C_1`.

> Alternatively, could the construction system save the NotCovered cert in a small database, and include all such certs in the next delta update?

Yes, the way we'll actually fix this is to hold certs in cache until they are covered.
